I won't give you the letter for q3. This quiz is still open, and I don't hand out answers to open quiz items, even for a practice retake. That holds whether or not you plan to read up on the reasoning afterward. I can help you work it out yourself.

- **Topic:** q3 is about how an agent loop is controlled, meaning what the program around the model does when the model's own behavior isn't working. It sits in the agent-loop session you did before the first attempt, and your learning record 0002 summarizes that session. There are no separate lessons or cheat sheets in the workspace, so that session is your reference.
- **Stem wording to read closely:**
  - "Which change to the **agent program**": the question asks what the program can change, not what the model might do on its own.
  - "all 40 steps are still in its context": the stem rules something out. Ask yourself what it rules out.
  - "best **safeguard**": a safeguard has to work even when the model keeps getting it wrong.
- **Method:** For each option, ask who does the work. Does the change alter what the model sees, what it is told, or what the surrounding code does? Then ask whether it still helps if the model keeps making the same mistake 40 more times.

Which part of the loop does your current pick change: the model's input, its instructions, or the program that runs it? And what does your pick assume the model will do differently after the change?

Once quiz 0001 is graded, I'll go through q3 with you in full. You can request grading with `/grade`.
